headline: mixed
texts: You have a workable base and some real gaps. Each fall below names the model to fix, not something you cannot do. Start with the confident errors, then the gaps, then the shaky items, and retake the module after those review cards.
Shaky: you know both tests but the order wobbled. Say it aloud: TSH and ultrasound first, scan only if TSH is low, FNAC for the nature of the nodule.
Shaky: the split mostly holds, but the nuclei-versus-invasion rule slipped on some stems. Ask which feature the tumour is defined by before reading the options.
Shaky: you know papillary leads, but some settings pulled you elsewhere. Check whether the stem says overall or relative, children, radiation or thyroglossal cyst.
Shaky: the routes mostly hold, but a site or list slipped. Derive the route from the cell: follicular invades vessels, so it goes by blood.
Shaky: you know the categories but a name or action got swapped. Pair each number with its word, then its action.
Shaky: you know the size bands but some cases defaulted to one operation. Walk the ladder: under 1 cm, 1 to 4 cm, over 4 cm or advanced.
Shaky: the radioiodine logic mostly holds, but one phase blurred. Keep the phases apart: high TSH to drive uptake, then suppression to starve residual tumour.
Shaky: you know the markers but the interpretation wobbled. Check antibodies before trusting Tg, and switch tests when iodine uptake is lost.
Shaky: most of the complications hold, but a nerve or order step slipped. Separate commonest from most feared, and pitch from hoarseness.
Shaky: the staging age and look-alikes mostly hold. Recheck that AJCC 8th uses 55, not 45.
You changed your mind on FNAC first and then held it on a later question. Keep reading whether the stem asks first or nature, since the old key can pull you back under time pressure.
You moved off follicular as the default and read the setting later. Keep checking overall versus relative; stems can flip on one phrase.
You changed your mind about cytology or frozen section diagnosing follicular cancer. Under pressure the papillary habit of reading nuclei on FNAC can return, so keep asking what the test can see.
You moved from papillae to nuclei as the test. Under exam pressure the name 'papillary' can pull you back, so check nuclei first.
You moved from the old key to NIFTP. Under pressure the older 'follicular variant is cancer' answer can return, so ask whether invasion is present.
You moved from 45 to 55. Under pressure the PYQ number can return, so ask which edition the stem uses.
You changed from one operation for every DTC to size and risk bands. Under pressure the classic total thyroidectomy key can return, so check size, nodes and extension.
You changed from ectopic thyroid to nodal metastasis. Under pressure the name can mislead again, so think by site: lateral neck, papillary node.
You reversed the routes at first, then held them. Under pressure, re-derive from invasion: follicular invades vessels, so it goes by blood.
You dropped nodes from the follicular set and later held it. Under pressure the familiar item can creep back in, so test each against blood spread and follicular-cell origin.
You moved from repeating the scan to FDG-PET. Under pressure, ask whether the tumour still takes up iodine.
You moved from radioiodine for all to radioiodine by risk. Under pressure 'standard adjuvant' can return, so check the ATA risk group.
You moved from operating on a benign report to follow-up. Under pressure, match category first, then action.
You swapped IV and V at first, then separated them. Under pressure tie each number to its word: IV follicular neoplasm, V suspicious.
You moved from the recurrent laryngeal nerve to the external branch for pitch loss. Under pressure the familiar nerve can return, so link pitch to cricothyroid.
You moved from nerve injury or bleeding to hypocalcaemia. Under pressure the dramatic complication can pull you back, so ask frequency.
You moved from the airway device to releasing the clot first. Under pressure the intubate-first reflex can return, so ask what is compressing the airway.
You reversed the TSH direction at first, then separated the phases. Under pressure ask whether the phase needs uptake or tumour starvation.
You moved from reading Tg alone to checking antibodies. Under pressure a low number can still reassure, so ask whether the assay can be trusted.
You swapped the markers at first, then separated them. Under pressure go by cell: follicular makes thyroglobulin, C cell makes calcitonin.

You tend to answer with the older PYQ key where current practice differs: FNAC first, total thyroidectomy for all, age 45, any follicular variant as cancer. Hold both: what PYQs expected and what is current.
You tend to miss the qualifier: iodine-deficient versus sufficient, low versus high risk, or antibodies present. Underline the qualifier in the stem before reading the options.
You tend to pick a test that cannot answer the question asked: cytology for invasion, or a repeat scan for refractory disease. Ask what each test can see, then climb the ladder.
You tend to confuse look-alikes: papillary architecture for papillary nuclei, or one laryngeal nerve for another. Before answering, name the one feature that separates the pair.
You tend to pair a name or marker with the wrong condition: lateral aberrant thyroid as ectopia, or calcitonin with DTC. Pair by site and cell of origin instead of by label.
You tend to reverse a mechanism: spread routes or the TSH direction around radioiodine. Predict from the cause first, such as invasion of vessels meaning blood spread, then check.
You tend to get the order wrong: operating on a benign report or intubating before releasing a clot. Ask what comes first and why before choosing.
You tapped Sure on at least two answers that were wrong. Those are the most useful errors, because a corrected confident error sticks best. Slow down on Sure answers and check the qualifier first.
You asked for hints or explanations often. That is a sound strategy while learning, but cold recall is what the exam tests. Retake the module and try each probe before opening any help.
Do the review cards in this order: confident errors first, then gaps, then shaky items. After each card, meet the idea again on a new question before moving on.
